text.title: Complete Massage Overview
text.summary: An overview of basic movement directions, body areas, and the sequence of a general massage.
text.goal: Use this card as a navigation map for the guide's sections and individual techniques.
text.imageAlt: Infographic showing basic massage techniques and body areas.
text.startingPosition: Open an individual technique for the body area you want to work on and follow its instructions.
instructions: Use this card as a general navigation overview.
Open individual techniques by body area for practical guidance.
Follow the pressure and safety notes provided for each technique.
text.direction: Movement direction depends on the selected technique and body area.
tips: Start with gentle techniques and progress gradually.
Use the receiver's comfort as the primary guide.
mistakes: Using the overview instead of the instructions for a specific technique.
Ignoring pain, inflammation, or damaged skin.
text.warning: This overview is not individualized medical advice.
text.telegramCaption: A basic map of massage areas and techniques. Detailed techniques are available in the PWA.

text.title: Longitudinal Back Stroking
text.summary: A gentle foundational technique in which both palms glide from the lower back toward the shoulders.
text.goal: Prepare the soft tissues for subsequent techniques while creating warmth and relaxation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of longitudinal back stroking without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down. Place both palms on the lower back on either side of the spine.
instructions: Place both palms gently on the lower back.
Glide both palms upward over the muscles on either side of the spine.
Near the upper back, gently move the hands outward.
Return down along the sides using minimal pressure.
text.direction: Primary movement: lower back to shoulders; return gently along the sides.
tips: Keep the movement symmetrical and unhurried.
mistakes: Strong direct pressure on the spine.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: A gentle foundational technique in which both palms glide from the lower back toward the shoulders.

text.title: Fan-Shaped Back Stroking
text.summary: The palms fan outward from the central back toward the sides in broad, gentle strokes.
text.goal: Warm a broad area of the back and distribute contact smoothly toward the sides.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of fan-shaped back stroking without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down. Place the palms near each other on the lower or middle back.
instructions: Begin with both palms near the center line without pressing on the spine.
Continue the arc toward the sides of the back.
Reduce pressure near the outer edge of the torso.
Return to the start and repeat the fan pattern on the next area.
text.direction: Movements fan outward from the center with a slight upward direction.
tips: Keep the arcs broad and even on both sides.
Reduce pressure near the edge of the torso.
mistakes: Using strokes that are too short or narrow.
Abrupt wrist turns at the side of the torso.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: The palms fan outward from the central back toward the sides in broad, gentle strokes.

text.title: Transverse Back Stroking
text.summary: Broad gentle passes move across the back muscles from the central area toward the sides.
text.goal: Introduce a different direction of gentle contact and prepare the lateral back for further work.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of transverse back stroking without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down. Position the palms on one side of the spine or symmetrically on both sides.
instructions: Place the palm on soft tissue next to the spine.
Glide across the muscles toward the side of the torso.
Reduce pressure as you approach the outer edge.
Return without pressure and repeat slightly above or below.
When using both hands, keep an even rhythm.
text.direction: From the central back toward the side of the torso, across the muscle region.
tips: Use the broad surface of the palm.
Keep the glide smooth without pinching the skin.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: Broad gentle passes move across the back muscles from the central area toward the sides.

text.title: Circular Palm Rubbing
text.summary: The palms make small, controlled circular movements over the soft tissues of the back.
text.goal: Increase local warmth and prepare the tissues for kneading without deep pressure.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of circular palm rubbing without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down. Keep the full palm in contact with the selected soft-tissue area.
instructions: Place the palm on the soft tissue of the back.
Make small circular movements without working directly over bony prominences.
Gradually move the circles to the neighboring area.
Avoid direct pressure on the spine and ribs.
text.direction: Small circles that gradually travel across the selected area.
tips: Keep the circles small and controlled.
Start lighter and increase pressure only when comfortable.
mistakes: Rubbing across the bony edge of the scapula.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: The palms make small, controlled circular movements over the soft tissues of the back.

text.title: Heel-of-Hand Rubbing
text.summary: The heel of the hand performs short, controlled rubbing movements over larger muscle areas of the back.
text.goal: Provide more focused work on larger soft-tissue areas while keeping pressure controlled.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of heel-of-hand rubbing without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down. Place the heel of the hand on a muscular area while keeping the fingers relaxed.
instructions: Place the heel of the hand on a soft muscular area.
Use short longitudinal strokes or small circles.
Move gradually instead of staying on one point for too long.
Control pressure with the whole arm rather than only the wrist.
Avoid the spine, scapular borders, and other bony prominences.
text.direction: Short longitudinal or small circular movements over a broad muscle mass.
tips: Keep the wrist in a neutral position.
Pressure can feel firm but should not be painful.
mistakes: Dropping full body weight onto one point.
Working over ribs or the spine.
Tense fingers and an overloaded wrist.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: The heel of the hand performs short, controlled rubbing movements over larger muscle areas of the back.

text.title: Longitudinal Back Kneading
text.summary: Soft tissue is gently gathered and worked along the muscle mass without sharp pinching.
text.goal: Gently work larger muscle areas after the tissues have been warmed up.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of longitudinal back kneading without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down. Warm the tissues first with stroking or rubbing.
instructions: Place both hands over a soft muscular area.
Gently gather the tissue between the palms and fingers without pinching the skin.
Move slightly higher along the muscle and repeat.
Keep a slow rhythm and avoid working directly on the spine.
text.direction: Progress gradually along the long axis of the muscle mass.
tips: Gather soft tissue rather than pinching only the skin.
mistakes: Deep work without warming the tissue first.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: Soft tissue is gently gathered and worked along the muscle mass without sharp pinching.

text.title: Transverse Back Kneading
text.summary: Both hands gently displace the muscle mass in opposite directions across its long axis.
text.goal: Vary the kneading pattern and gently mobilize larger areas of muscle tissue.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of transverse back kneading without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down. Warm the area first and place both hands over the muscle mass.
instructions: Place the hands on opposite sides of the selected muscular area.
Gently shift the tissue toward you with one hand and away with the other.
Release pressure without abruptly losing contact.
Move to the neighboring area and repeat.
Do not perform the movement directly over the spine or bony borders.
text.direction: Alternating displacement of soft tissue across the muscle mass.
tips: Use the palm and fingers together.
Keep the movement small and comfortable.
mistakes: Twisting only the skin instead of soft tissue.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: Both hands gently displace the muscle mass in opposite directions across its long axis.

text.title: Trapezius Muscle Work
text.summary: Gentle palm-and-finger work over the upper shoulder girdle without pressing on the neck or bony structures.
text.goal: Reduce the subjective feeling of tension in the upper shoulder girdle and encourage relaxation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of trapezius muscle work without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down or sits comfortably. Keep the shoulders relaxed and the neck neutral.
instructions: Place the palm on the soft part of the upper shoulder.
Use a few gentle strokes from the base of the neck toward the shoulder.
Add small circular movements over the muscle.
If comfortable, gently compress the muscle between the fingers and heel of the hand.
Reduce pressure near the neck and bony landmarks.
text.direction: From the base of the neck toward the shoulder; local circles stay on soft tissue.
tips: Ask the person to relax the shoulders.
Use less pressure near the base of the neck.
mistakes: Pressure on the side or front of the neck.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: Gentle palm-and-finger work over the upper shoulder girdle without pressing on the neck or bony structures.

text.title: Work Around the Shoulder Blades
text.summary: Gentle movements work the muscles around the shoulder blade without heavy pressure over its bony borders.
text.goal: Work the soft tissues around the scapular region while staying comfortable around bony landmarks.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of work around the shoulder blades without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down with the arm relaxed alongside the body. Keep the shoulder blade in a natural position.
instructions: Begin with gentle strokes around the scapular area.
Use the fingers or palm to make small circles over soft tissue near the scapular borders.
Progress around the outer and lower surrounding muscle tissue.
Do not press directly on the bony edge of the shoulder blade.
text.direction: Follow the soft tissue around the scapular outline without pressing on the bone itself.
tips: Clearly distinguish soft tissue from the bony border.
mistakes: Heavy pressure on the scapular border or spine.
Trying to work deeply under the scapula without specific training.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: Gentle movements work the muscles around the shoulder blade without heavy pressure over its bony borders.

text.title: Gentle Lumbar Area Work
text.summary: Broad, gentle movements are applied to the muscles of the lower back without deep pressure.
text.goal: Provide comfortable, relaxing contact to the lower back as part of a general massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of gentle lumbar area work without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down. Use support under the abdomen or lower legs if needed for comfort.
instructions: Place the broad surface of the palms over the lower-back muscles.
Use slow strokes upward and slightly outward.
Add small palm circles only over soft tissue.
Keep the pressure light to moderate.
Avoid strong vertical pressure and painful areas.
text.direction: Upward and outward over the soft tissues of the lower back.
tips: Reduce pressure or stop immediately if discomfort appears.
mistakes: Strong pressure directly over the spinal midline.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: Broad, gentle movements are applied to the muscles of the lower back without deep pressure.

text.title: Gentle Back Vibration
text.summary: The palms create light rhythmic oscillations over soft tissue without striking or abrupt movement.
text.goal: Add a brief, rhythmic relaxation technique near the end of the massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of gentle back vibration without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down. Keep the palm fully in contact with a soft muscular area.
instructions: Place the palm on a soft area of the back.
Create small, quick oscillations without striking.
Continue for a few seconds, then move gently to the next area.
text.direction: Small oscillations in place, gradually moving across soft tissue.
tips: Avoid tensing the practitioner's wrist and shoulder.
mistakes: Prolonged vibration over one sensitive spot.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: The palms create light rhythmic oscillations over soft tissue without striking or abrupt movement.

text.title: Finishing Back Stroking
text.summary: Very gentle, long gliding passes finish the session and gradually reduce the intensity of contact.
text.goal: Bring the back massage to a gradual close and transition from active techniques to calm contact.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of finishing back stroking without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person remains relaxed in a face-down position. Place the palms on the lower or middle back.
instructions: Place both palms on the back with light pressure.
Glide upward smoothly over soft tissue.
Move the hands outward toward the sides.
Return downward with almost no pressure.
Reduce pressure and pace slightly with each pass.
Finish with a brief, calm palm contact.
text.direction: Long smooth upward passes with a gentle return along the sides.
mistakes: Speeding up at the very end.
Using strong pressure during the finishing phase.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
text.telegramCaption: Very gentle, long gliding passes finish the session and gradually reduce the intensity of contact.

text.title: Gentle Posterior Neck Stroking
text.summary: A very gentle introductory technique for the back of the neck, with the palms or finger pads gliding from the base of the skull toward the shoulders.
text.goal: Establish comfortable contact, gently warm superficial tissues, and prepare the neck and shoulder area for later techniques.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of gentle posterior neck stroking without text labels.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down comfortably or sits with the arms and head supported. Keep the neck in a neutral position without extending it backward.
instructions: Place the palms or finger pads on either side of the posterior midline of the neck.
Begin with very light contact near the base of the skull.
Glide smoothly downward over the soft tissues toward the tops of the shoulders.
Near the shoulders, gently move the hands outward.
text.direction: The main movement travels from the base of the skull down toward the shoulders, staying on soft tissue beside the spine.
tips: Keep the neck in a neutral position.
Make the first passes especially gentle.
mistakes: Strong pressure directly over the cervical vertebrae.
Abrupt movements or extending the head backward.
Pressure on the front or side of the neck.
text.warning: Do not massage the front of the neck or the carotid area. Stop if pain, dizziness, numbness, or unusual symptoms occur. Neck injuries or medical conditions require professional advice.
text.telegramCaption: A gentle introductory stroke from the base of the skull toward the shoulders.

text.title: Longitudinal Neck Stroking
text.summary: Both hands make parallel, smooth passes along the back of the neck without applying direct pressure to the spine.
text.goal: Gently relax superficial tissues and establish a calm rhythm before rubbing or kneading techniques.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of longitudinal stroking along the posterior neck with both hands.
text.startingPosition: The head is supported and the neck remains neutral. The hands rest on either side of the posterior midline.
instructions: Place both hands symmetrically beside the spine.
Glide along the neck in a longitudinal direction.
Maintain even speed and light pressure.
Avoid pressing directly over the spinous processes.
text.direction: Parallel longitudinal movements over the soft tissues along the back of the neck.
tips: Reduce pressure near the base of the skull.
mistakes: Uneven speed between the two hands.
Using deep pressure in the small neck area.
text.warning: The cervical region requires gentle work. Avoid deep pressure when pain, recent injury, or neurological symptoms are present.
text.telegramCaption: Parallel gentle passes along the posterior neck.

text.title: Neck-to-Shoulder Stroking
text.summary: A smooth stroke begins at the posterior neck and continues outward along the top line of the shoulders.
text.goal: Connect neck and shoulder work while gently distributing contact across the upper trapezius.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of stroking from the posterior neck toward the shoulders.
text.startingPosition: The person lies or sits in a stable position with relaxed shoulders. The hands begin near the base of the neck.
instructions: Place the hands near the base of the neck on either side of the spine.
Continue along the upper shoulders toward the outside.
Gradually reduce pressure near the shoulder joints.
text.direction: From the base of the neck outward along the upper shoulder line.
tips: Follow the natural contour of the shoulder girdle.
Do not lift the person's shoulders with the movement.
mistakes: Excessive pressure at the base of the neck.
text.warning: Do not work through acute pain, inflammation, or recent shoulder-girdle injury.
text.telegramCaption: A smooth transition from the base of the neck outward along the shoulders.

text.title: Circular Shoulder Rubbing
text.summary: Small controlled circular movements are applied to the soft tissues over the upper shoulders and upper trapezius.
text.goal: Gradually increase local warmth and prepare the soft tissues for more pronounced kneading.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of circular rubbing over the upper shoulder region.
text.startingPosition: The shoulders are fully relaxed. The finger pads or heel of the hand rest on the soft tissues over the upper shoulder.
instructions: Place the hand on the soft part of the shoulder rather than a bony prominence.
Make small circular movements that move the tissue rather than sliding over the skin.
Progress slowly along the upper shoulder.
text.direction: Small circles over the upper shoulder soft tissues, gradually progressing along the muscle.
tips: The circle should move the soft tissue rather than rub the skin.
mistakes: Pressing onto the acromion or other bony prominences.
Using circles that are too large or too fast.
text.warning: Reduce pressure or stop if the area becomes painful. Do not rub inflamed or damaged skin.
text.telegramCaption: Controlled circular movements over the soft tissues of the upper shoulders.

text.title: Upper Trapezius Kneading
text.summary: The soft tissue of the upper trapezius is gently lifted and rhythmically kneaded between the fingers and palm.
text.goal: Work the bulk of the upper trapezius without pressing on the cervical vertebrae or bony shoulder structures.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of kneading the upper trapezius.
text.startingPosition: The shoulder is relaxed. The practitioner's hand rests on the muscular ridge between the base of the neck and shoulder.
instructions: Locate the soft muscular area between the neck and shoulder.
Gently grasp the tissue between the fingers and heel of the hand.
Lift slightly and compress the muscle comfortably.
Release the pressure without losing contact.
Progress in small sections along the muscle.
text.direction: Work progressively along the muscular ridge from the base of the neck toward the shoulder.
tips: Grasp muscle tissue rather than pinching the skin.
mistakes: Moving onto the side of the neck.
text.warning: Avoid deep kneading with acute pain, recent injury, or neurological symptoms. Stop if pressure produces radiating pain.
text.telegramCaption: Controlled kneading of the soft upper trapezius.

text.title: Gentle Shoulder Compression
text.summary: The palms gently and rhythmically compress the muscular tissues over the upper shoulders without sharp pinching.
text.goal: Provide even, comfortable compression to the soft tissues of the shoulder girdle.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of gentle compression over the upper shoulder muscles.
text.startingPosition: The shoulders are lowered and relaxed. The hands rest over the soft upper shoulder tissues.
instructions: Enclose the soft shoulder tissue with the palm and fingers.
Gradually increase pressure to a comfortable level.
text.direction: Compression is directed into the soft shoulder tissue without moving toward the front or side of the neck.
tips: Make sure the person is not tensing or lifting the shoulders.
mistakes: Pressing with the fingers into the side of the neck.
text.warning: Do not compress areas with swelling, recent injury, marked tenderness, or inflammation.
text.telegramCaption: Gentle rhythmic compression of the upper shoulder muscles.

text.title: Upper Shoulder Line Gliding
text.summary: Smooth passes follow the soft tissues along the upper shoulder line from the base of the neck outward.
text.goal: Move progressively along the upper shoulder line while supporting relaxation of the upper trapezius.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of a smooth glide along the upper shoulder line.
text.startingPosition: The shoulders are relaxed, with the practitioner's hands resting over the soft tissue between the base of the neck and outer shoulder.
instructions: Begin on the soft tissue near the base of the neck.
Glide the palm or finger pads outward along the upper shoulder line.
Pass around bony prominences without extra pressure.
Reduce pressure near the shoulder joint.
text.direction: From the base of the neck outward along the upper shoulder line.
tips: Follow soft tissue rather than bony landmarks.
Keep the movement long and continuous.
mistakes: Applying strong pressure near the base of the neck.
text.warning: Do not perform this technique over acute localized pain or a recent shoulder injury.
text.telegramCaption: A smooth glide from the base of the neck outward along the upper shoulder line.

text.title: Gentle Work at the Base of the Skull
text.summary: The finger pads make gentle contact with the muscular tissues just below the occipital bone, without pressing on bone or the front of the neck.
text.goal: Work delicately around the small suboccipital area using minimal pressure.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of gentle contact with muscles at the base of the skull.
text.startingPosition: The head is fully supported and remains neutral. The fingers rest just below the occipital bone at the back of the head.
instructions: Locate the soft tissues immediately below the occipital bone.
Place the finger pads symmetrically on either side of the midline.
Hold for a few seconds without digging in.
Release smoothly and move to a nearby small area.
text.direction: Small local contacts below the occipital bone on either side of the midline.
areasText: muscles at the base of the skull
mistakes: Pressing directly onto the occipital bone.
Extending or rotating the head while applying pressure.
text.warning: Avoid this technique after recent head or neck injury, with marked dizziness, neurological symptoms, or unexplained severe headache. Do not press on the front or side of the neck.
text.telegramCaption: Very gentle local contact with the muscles just below the base of the skull.

text.title: Circular Movements in the Occipital Area
text.summary: The finger pads make very small, slow circles over the soft tissues just below the occipital line.
text.goal: Gently mobilize superficial soft tissues in the occipital region without deep focal pressure.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of small circular movements in the occipital area.
text.startingPosition: The head is supported. The fingers rest on soft tissue below the occipital bone rather than on the bone itself.
instructions: Place the finger pads on soft tissue below the occipital line.
Make small, slow circles that move with the tissue.
Move to a nearby area and repeat.
Work symmetrically on both sides of the midline.
text.direction: Small local circles below the occipital line.
tips: Reduce pressure immediately if discomfort appears.
mistakes: Sliding over the hair instead of moving the soft tissue.
text.warning: Do not perform after a recent head or neck injury or with marked dizziness, neurological symptoms, or unexplained severe headache.
text.telegramCaption: Small, slow circles over the soft tissues below the occipital line.

text.title: Bilateral Shoulder Kneading
text.summary: Both hands perform gentle rhythmic kneading over the upper shoulders at the same time, maintaining symmetry and comfortable pressure.
text.goal: Work the muscular tissues of the right and left shoulder girdle evenly.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of bilateral kneading over the upper shoulders.
text.startingPosition: Both shoulders are relaxed. The palms rest on the muscular tissues over the upper shoulders.
instructions: Place both hands symmetrically on the soft shoulder tissues.
Gently grasp and slightly lift the muscle.
Apply a smooth compression with both hands at the same time.
Repeat with the same rhythm on both sides.
text.direction: Symmetrical kneading over the upper shoulders without moving onto the front of the neck.
tips: Compare the response of the right and left sides.
mistakes: Kneading too deeply near the base of the neck.
text.warning: Do not continue without professional advice if there is marked one-sided pain, recent injury, numbness, or radiating pain.
text.telegramCaption: Simultaneous gentle kneading over both upper shoulders.

text.title: Gentle Shoulder Vibration
text.summary: The palms stay in contact with the shoulder muscles while creating a small, gentle rhythmic vibration without percussion.
text.goal: Add a brief, gentle rhythmic technique before finishing work on the shoulder girdle.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of gentle vibration over the upper shoulders.
text.startingPosition: The palms rest loosely on the soft tissues of the upper shoulders, with the hands and forearms relaxed.
instructions: Place the palms on the soft upper shoulder tissues.
Create a small, rapid vibration through the palms.
Do not turn the movement into percussion or strong shaking.
Stop smoothly after a few seconds.
text.direction: Fine vibration is transmitted through the palms into the soft shoulder tissues.
tips: Let the movement come from relaxed hands.
mistakes: Shaking the head and neck strongly.
Continuing vibration when it causes discomfort.
text.warning: Avoid vibration with acute pain, recent injury, marked dizziness, or whenever the movement triggers unpleasant symptoms.
text.telegramCaption: Brief, gentle vibration through the palms over the upper shoulders.

text.title: Finishing Neck and Shoulder Stroking
text.summary: Long, light passes connect the posterior neck and shoulders while gradually reducing the intensity of contact.
text.goal: Finish the sequence calmly and reduce intensity after more active techniques.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram of finishing stroking over the posterior neck and shoulders.
text.startingPosition: The neck and shoulders are relaxed. The palms make gentle contact with the posterior neck and upper shoulders.
instructions: Begin with light contact near the base of the skull or base of the neck.
Glide downward along the posterior neck.
Continue outward over the upper shoulders.
Reduce pressure slightly with each following pass.
Finish with several very light, slow strokes.
text.direction: From the posterior neck toward the shoulders with gradually decreasing pressure.
text.warning: Finishing strokes should never be performed through pain. Stop if dizziness, numbness, or other unusual symptoms appear.
text.telegramCaption: Long, light passes over the neck and shoulders with gradually decreasing pressure.

text.title: Forearm Stroking
text.summary: Gentle longitudinal passes over the forearm from the wrist toward the elbow.
text.goal: Warm the superficial forearm tissues.
text.startingPosition: The arm rests on support and the hand is relaxed.
instructions: Place the palm above the wrist.
text.direction: From the wrist toward the elbow over soft tissue.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, inflammation, or impaired sensation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: forearm stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Gentle longitudinal passes over the forearm from the wrist toward the elbow.

text.title: Longitudinal Upper-Arm Stroking
text.summary: The palm glides over the upper arm from the elbow toward the shoulder.
text.goal: Prepare the upper-arm muscles for later work.
text.startingPosition: The arm is relaxed and supported.
instructions: Glide upward over the muscular upper arm.
Do not press on the joint.
text.direction: From elbow toward shoulder.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, inflammation, or impaired sensation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: longitudinal upper-arm stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The palm glides over the upper arm from the elbow toward the shoulder.

text.title: Circular Forearm Rubbing
text.summary: Small circles are applied over the muscular forearm.
text.goal: Warm the soft tissues before kneading.
text.startingPosition: The forearm is comfortably supported.
instructions: Place the finger pads on muscle.
Make small circles that move with the tissue.
text.direction: Small circles over soft tissue.
tips: Move tissue rather than rubbing skin.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, inflammation, or impaired sensation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: circular forearm rubbing, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Small circles are applied over the muscular forearm.

text.title: Forearm Kneading
text.summary: The muscular tissue is gently grasped and rhythmically kneaded.
text.goal: Work the forearm muscles within a comfortable range.
text.startingPosition: The forearm rests on support.
instructions: Grasp it with the palm and fingers.
text.direction: Along the muscular forearm.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, inflammation, or impaired sensation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: forearm kneading, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The muscular tissue is gently grasped and rhythmically kneaded.

text.title: Upper-Arm Kneading
text.summary: The upper-arm muscle is gently compressed and released between the palm and fingers.
text.goal: Work the larger upper-arm muscles.
text.startingPosition: The arm is fully relaxed.
instructions: Place the hand on the muscular upper arm.
text.direction: Along the muscular upper arm.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, inflammation, or impaired sensation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: upper-arm kneading, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The upper-arm muscle is gently compressed and released between the palm and fingers.

text.title: Gentle Work Around the Elbow
text.summary: Very light movements are made around the elbow over soft tissue.
text.goal: Connect upper-arm and forearm work.
text.startingPosition: The elbow is slightly bent and supported.
instructions: Stroke the soft tissue around the joint.
text.direction: Around the joint over soft tissue.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, inflammation, or impaired sensation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: gentle work around the elbow, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Very light movements are made around the elbow over soft tissue.

text.title: Palm Massage
text.summary: The thumb or finger pads gently work the muscular palm.
text.goal: Relax the soft tissues of the hand after activity.
text.startingPosition: The hand rests palm-up.
instructions: Make small circles over the fleshy palm.
text.direction: Over the soft areas of the palm.
tips: Support the hand with the other hand.
Do not press with the nail.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, inflammation, or impaired sensation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: palm massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The thumb or finger pads gently work the muscular palm.

text.title: Dorsal Hand Stroking
text.summary: Very light longitudinal movements are made between bony and tendon structures.
text.goal: Gently work the back of the hand.
text.startingPosition: The hand is supported with the back facing upward.
instructions: Move from the wrist toward the fingers.
text.direction: From wrist toward the finger bases.
tips: Use less pressure than on the palm.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, inflammation, or impaired sensation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: dorsal hand stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Very light longitudinal movements are made between bony and tendon structures.

text.title: Finger Massage
text.summary: Each finger is gently stroked from base to tip without forceful traction.
text.goal: Finish hand work with gentle finger contact.
text.startingPosition: The hand is supported and the fingers are relaxed.
instructions: Hold one finger with a broad, gentle grip.
Do not pull or twist the joint.
text.direction: From the base of the finger toward the tip.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, inflammation, or impaired sensation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: finger massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Each finger is gently stroked from base to tip without forceful traction.

text.title: Finishing Arm Stroking
text.summary: Long, light passes connect the hand, forearm, and upper arm.
text.goal: Gradually reduce intensity and finish the arm massage.
text.startingPosition: The whole arm is relaxed and supported.
instructions: Continue over the upper arm while avoiding joints.
text.direction: From the hand upward along the arm.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, inflammation, or impaired sensation.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: finishing arm stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Long, light passes connect the hand, forearm, and upper arm.

text.title: Anterior Thigh Stroking
text.summary: Long smooth passes over the front of the thigh from above the knee upward.
text.goal: Warm the large thigh muscles.
text.startingPosition: The leg rests comfortably and relaxed.
instructions: Place the palm on the soft thigh tissue.
Do not press the joint or groin.
text.direction: From above the knee upward over soft tissue.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: anterior thigh stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Long smooth passes over the front of the thigh from above the knee upward.

text.title: Posterior Thigh Stroking
text.summary: Smooth passes over the back of the thigh while avoiding pressure behind the knee.
text.goal: Gently warm the posterior thigh muscles.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down with the leg relaxed.
instructions: Begin above the back of the knee.
Glide upward over the posterior thigh.
Do not press behind the knee.
Reduce pressure near the gluteal fold.
text.direction: Upward along the posterior thigh.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: posterior thigh stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Smooth passes over the back of the thigh while avoiding pressure behind the knee.

text.title: Lateral Thigh Gliding
text.summary: Long light passes over the soft tissues of the outer thigh.
text.goal: Gently include the lateral thigh in the sequence.
text.startingPosition: The leg is supported and relaxed.
instructions: Place the palm on the outer thigh.
text.direction: Longitudinally along the outer thigh.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: lateral thigh gliding, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Long light passes over the soft tissues of the outer thigh.

text.title: Circular Thigh Rubbing
text.summary: Controlled circular movements over the large thigh muscles.
text.goal: Gradually warm soft tissue before kneading.
text.startingPosition: The leg rests stably and relaxed.
instructions: Place the palm on the muscular thigh.
Make small circles that move with tissue.
text.direction: Small circles over the thigh muscles.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: circular thigh rubbing, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Controlled circular movements over the large thigh muscles.

text.title: Thigh Kneading
text.summary: The large thigh muscles are gently grasped, compressed, and released.
text.goal: Work the thigh muscles within a comfortable range.
text.startingPosition: The leg is fully relaxed.
text.direction: Over the major thigh muscles.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: thigh kneading, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The large thigh muscles are gently grasped, compressed, and released.

text.title: Calf Stroking
text.summary: The palms glide upward over the calf without pressing on the Achilles tendon or behind the knee.
text.goal: Gently warm the calf muscle.
text.startingPosition: The leg is relaxed and the foot supported.
instructions: Do not press behind the knee.
text.direction: Upward along the calf muscle.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: calf stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The palms glide upward over the calf without pressing on the Achilles tendon or behind the knee.

text.title: Calf Kneading
text.summary: The calf muscle is gently compressed and released between the palm and fingers.
text.goal: Work the calf after gentle warming.
text.startingPosition: The leg is relaxed and supported.
text.direction: Along the muscular calf from lower to upper areas.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: calf kneading, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The calf muscle is gently compressed and released between the palm and fingers.

text.title: Gentle Shin Stroking
text.summary: Light passes are made over the soft tissues beside the shin bone.
text.goal: Include the lower leg gently without pressing on bone.
text.startingPosition: The leg is relaxed and supported.
instructions: Locate soft tissue beside the shin.
Reduce pressure near ankle and knee.
text.direction: Longitudinally over the soft tissues of the lower leg.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: gentle shin stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Light passes are made over the soft tissues beside the shin bone.

text.title: Gentle Work Around the Ankle
text.summary: Very light movements are made around the ankle over soft tissue.
text.goal: Create a transition between lower leg and foot.
text.startingPosition: The foot and lower leg are supported.
instructions: Stroke soft tissue around the joint.
text.direction: Around the joint over soft tissue.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: gentle work around the ankle, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Very light movements are made around the ankle over soft tissue.

text.title: Superficial Gluteal Stroking
text.summary: Broad palm strokes are applied over the muscular gluteal region with clear consent and appropriate draping.
text.goal: Gently include the gluteal muscles in the sequence.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down; consent is obtained and only the necessary working area is exposed.
instructions: Make smooth passes over the muscular area.
text.direction: Broad movements over the muscular gluteal region.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: superficial gluteal stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Broad palm strokes are applied over the muscular gluteal region with clear consent and appropriate draping.

text.title: Circular Gluteal Rubbing
text.summary: Broad controlled circles are applied over the muscular gluteal region with consent and appropriate draping.
text.goal: Gradually warm the large gluteal muscles.
text.startingPosition: The person lies face down; only the necessary area is exposed.
instructions: Place the heel of the hand on muscle.
Avoid the sacrum and pelvic bones.
text.direction: Circular movements over the muscular region.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: circular gluteal rubbing, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Broad controlled circles are applied over the muscular gluteal region with consent and appropriate draping.

text.title: Finishing Lower-Leg Stroking
text.summary: Long light passes over the lower leg gradually reduce intensity.
text.goal: Finish lower-leg work calmly.
text.startingPosition: The leg and foot are supported.
instructions: Begin near the top of the foot.
Glide upward over lower-leg soft tissue.
text.direction: From the foot upward over lower-leg soft tissue.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: finishing lower-leg stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Long light passes over the lower leg gradually reduce intensity.

text.title: Whole-Leg Long Stroking
text.summary: Long continuous passes connect the lower leg and thigh while avoiding joints and the back of the knee.
text.goal: Connect separate leg regions into one sequence.
text.startingPosition: The entire leg rests stably and relaxed.
instructions: Move upward, reducing pressure near the knee.
Do not press behind the knee.
text.direction: Upward over the soft tissues of the leg.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: whole-leg long stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Long continuous passes connect the lower leg and thigh while avoiding joints and the back of the knee.

text.title: Finishing Leg Stroking
text.summary: Very light long passes over the leg gradually reduce contact intensity.
text.goal: Finish the leg massage calmly.
text.startingPosition: The leg is relaxed and supported.
instructions: Avoid joints and the back of the knee.
text.direction: Over the leg soft tissues with decreasing pressure.
text.warning: Do not massage with acute pain, recent injury, marked swelling, or inflammation. One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, or calf pain should be medically assessed before massage.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: finishing leg stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Very light long passes over the leg gradually reduce contact intensity.

text.title: General Foot Stroking
text.summary: Light palm strokes over the sole and top of the foot.
text.goal: Warm the foot gently and assess comfort.
text.startingPosition: The foot is fully supported.
instructions: Work the top of the foot very lightly.
text.direction: From heel toward toes over soft tissue.
text.warning: Do not massage with recent injury, marked swelling, ulcers, infection, severe pain, or impaired sensation unless medically advised.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: general foot stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Light palm strokes over the sole and top of the foot.

text.title: Longitudinal Sole Gliding
text.summary: The broad thumb pad glides along the sole from heel toward the forefoot.
text.goal: Gently work the longitudinal regions of the sole.
text.startingPosition: The foot is supported.
instructions: Glide the thumb pad along the sole.
Do not dig into painful points.
text.direction: From heel toward the forefoot.
text.warning: Do not massage with recent injury, marked swelling, ulcers, infection, severe pain, or impaired sensation unless medically advised.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: longitudinal sole gliding, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The broad thumb pad glides along the sole from heel toward the forefoot.

text.title: Circular Heel Rubbing
text.summary: Small circles are made over the soft tissues around the heel.
text.goal: Warm the heel tissues gently.
text.startingPosition: The heel is supported.
instructions: Place the hand or fingers on the soft heel tissue.
text.direction: Circular movements over soft heel tissue.
text.warning: Do not massage with recent injury, marked swelling, ulcers, infection, severe pain, or impaired sensation unless medically advised.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: circular heel rubbing, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Small circles are made over the soft tissues around the heel.

text.title: Gentle Arch Work
text.summary: The broad thumb pad glides along the soft tissues of the arch.
text.goal: Gently work the foot arch.
text.startingPosition: The foot is supported with the sole facing the practitioner.
instructions: Place the thumb pad on the arch.
text.direction: Along the soft tissues of the arch.
text.warning: Do not massage with recent injury, marked swelling, ulcers, infection, severe pain, or impaired sensation unless medically advised.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: gentle arch work, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The broad thumb pad glides along the soft tissues of the arch.

text.title: Circular Forefoot Rubbing
text.summary: Small circles are applied to the soft tissues under the bases of the toes.
text.goal: Warm the forefoot gently.
text.startingPosition: The foot is supported.
instructions: Place the fingers under the toe bases.
text.direction: Small circles over forefoot soft tissue.
text.warning: Do not massage with recent injury, marked swelling, ulcers, infection, severe pain, or impaired sensation unless medically advised.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: circular forefoot rubbing, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Small circles are applied to the soft tissues under the bases of the toes.

text.title: Gentle Toe Work
text.summary: Each toe is gently stroked without forceful traction or twisting.
text.goal: Finish forefoot work gently.
text.startingPosition: The foot is supported.
instructions: Hold one toe with a broad gentle grip.
Do not pull or twist the joint.
text.direction: From the base of each toe toward the tip.
text.warning: Do not massage with recent injury, marked swelling, ulcers, infection, severe pain, or impaired sensation unless medically advised.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: gentle toe work, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Each toe is gently stroked without forceful traction or twisting.

text.title: Dorsal Foot Stroking
text.summary: Very light passes are made between bony and tendon structures on the top of the foot.
text.goal: Gently work the top of the foot.
text.startingPosition: The foot is supported.
instructions: Place the fingers on the top of the foot.
Move from toes toward the ankle.
Do not press on ankle bones.
text.direction: From toes toward the ankle.
text.warning: Do not massage with recent injury, marked swelling, ulcers, infection, severe pain, or impaired sensation unless medically advised.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: dorsal foot stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Very light passes are made between bony and tendon structures on the top of the foot.

text.title: Gentle Foot Compression
text.summary: The hands gently enclose the foot and apply brief even compression.
text.goal: Provide calm, even pressure to the foot.
text.startingPosition: The foot is fully supported between the hands.
instructions: Place the hands on both sides of the foot.
text.direction: Even compression through the palms.
text.warning: Do not massage with recent injury, marked swelling, ulcers, infection, severe pain, or impaired sensation unless medically advised.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: gentle foot compression, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The hands gently enclose the foot and apply brief even compression.

text.title: Foot-to-Ankle Transition
text.summary: Light movements connect the foot with the soft tissues around the ankle.
text.goal: Connect foot work with lower-leg work.
text.startingPosition: The foot is supported.
instructions: Begin on the top of the foot.
text.direction: From the foot toward soft tissue around the ankle.
text.warning: Do not massage with recent injury, marked swelling, ulcers, infection, severe pain, or impaired sensation unless medically advised.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: foot-to-ankle transition, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Light movements connect the foot with the soft tissues around the ankle.

text.title: Finishing Foot Stroking
text.summary: Very light smooth passes gradually reduce contact intensity.
text.goal: Finish the foot massage calmly.
text.startingPosition: The foot is relaxed and supported.
instructions: Stroke the sole with broad contact.
Move to the top very lightly.
text.direction: Over the whole foot with decreasing pressure.
text.warning: Do not massage with recent injury, marked swelling, ulcers, infection, severe pain, or impaired sensation unless medically advised.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: finishing foot stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Very light smooth passes gradually reduce contact intensity.

text.title: Forehead Stroking
text.summary: Very light movements travel from the center of the forehead toward the temples.
text.goal: Gently relax the superficial forehead tissues.
text.startingPosition: The head is supported.
instructions: Place the finger pads at the center of the forehead.
text.direction: From the center of the forehead toward the temples.
text.warning: Do not massage damaged or inflamed skin. Stop with dizziness, worsening headache, pain, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: forehead stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Very light movements travel from the center of the forehead toward the temples.

text.title: Circular Temple Movements
text.summary: The finger pads make small slow circles over the temple region.
text.goal: Provide a gentle relaxing contact.
text.startingPosition: The head is supported.
instructions: Place the finger pads on the temples.
text.direction: Small circles over the temples.
text.warning: Do not massage damaged or inflamed skin. Stop with dizziness, worsening headache, pain, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: circular temple movements, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The finger pads make small slow circles over the temple region.

text.title: Gentle Jaw-Muscle Work
text.summary: Small gentle circles are applied over the muscular cheek near the masseter.
text.goal: Gently relax superficial tissues around the jaw.
text.startingPosition: The jaw is relaxed and the teeth are not clenched.
instructions: Ask the person to relax the jaw.
Place the fingers over the soft cheek tissue.
Do not press on the joint.
text.direction: Small circles over the muscular cheek tissue.
text.warning: Do not massage damaged or inflamed skin. Stop with dizziness, worsening headache, pain, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: gentle jaw-muscle work, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Small gentle circles are applied over the muscular cheek near the masseter.

text.title: Circular Scalp Massage
text.summary: The finger pads gently move the scalp in small circles.
text.goal: Gently relax the scalp tissues.
text.startingPosition: The head is stably supported.
instructions: Place the finger pads on the scalp.
Make small circles that move with the skin.
Do not scratch with the nails.
text.direction: Small circles over the scalp.
text.warning: Do not massage damaged or inflamed skin. Stop with dizziness, worsening headache, pain, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: circular scalp massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The finger pads gently move the scalp in small circles.

text.title: Gentle Head Compression
text.summary: The palms gently contact the sides of the head with very light even pressure.
text.goal: Provide calm static contact.
text.startingPosition: The head is fully supported.
instructions: Place the palms on the sides of the head.
Do not press the temples or ears.
text.direction: Static pressure through broad palm contact.
text.warning: Do not massage damaged or inflamed skin. Stop with dizziness, worsening headache, pain, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: gentle head compression, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The palms gently contact the sides of the head with very light even pressure.

text.title: Light Cheek Stroking
text.summary: Very light symmetrical movements travel from the center of the face outward.
text.goal: Gently finish facial work.
text.startingPosition: The skin is clean and the head supported.
instructions: Place the fingers near the center of the cheeks.
Avoid pressure on the eye sockets.
text.direction: From the center of the face outward.
text.warning: Do not massage damaged or inflamed skin. Stop with dizziness, worsening headache, pain, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: light cheek stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Very light symmetrical movements travel from the center of the face outward.

text.title: Gentle Stroking Around the Ears
text.summary: Light movements are made around the outer ear over soft tissue.
text.goal: Connect temple and occipital work.
text.startingPosition: The head is supported.
instructions: Use the finger pads around the outer ear.
Do not press into the ear canal.
text.direction: Around the outer ear over soft tissue.
text.warning: Do not massage damaged or inflamed skin. Stop with dizziness, worsening headache, pain, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: gentle stroking around the ears, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Light movements are made around the outer ear over soft tissue.

text.title: Finishing Head and Face Stroking
text.summary: Very light passes over the forehead, temples, and scalp gradually reduce intensity.
text.goal: Finish head and face work calmly.
text.startingPosition: The head is supported and the person relaxed.
instructions: Begin with a light forehead stroke.
text.direction: From the center of the forehead outward and then to the scalp.
text.warning: Do not massage damaged or inflamed skin. Stop with dizziness, worsening headache, pain, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: finishing head and face stroking, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Very light passes over the forehead, temples, and scalp gradually reduce intensity.

text.title: Posterior Neck Self-Massage
text.summary: The fingers glide gently down the back of the neck toward the shoulders without pressure on the front of the neck.
text.goal: Gently ease the feeling of tension after static posture.
text.startingPosition: Sit stably, lower the shoulders, and keep the head neutral.
instructions: Place the fingers on the back of the neck.
Glide gently downward toward the shoulders.
Do not press the front or side of the neck.
text.direction: Down the back of the neck toward the shoulders.
text.warning: Stop self-massage with pain, numbness, weakness, dizziness, radiating sensations, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: posterior neck self-massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The fingers glide gently down the back of the neck toward the shoulders without pressure on the front of the neck.

text.title: Shoulder Self-Massage
text.summary: One hand gently kneads the opposite upper shoulder with a broad grip.
text.goal: Work the upper trapezius gently on yourself.
text.startingPosition: Sit comfortably and lower the shoulders.
instructions: Place one hand on the opposite shoulder.
Do not move onto the side of the neck.
text.direction: Over the soft upper shoulder.
text.warning: Stop self-massage with pain, numbness, weakness, dizziness, radiating sensations, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: shoulder self-massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: One hand gently kneads the opposite upper shoulder with a broad grip.

text.title: Forearm Self-Massage
text.summary: The free hand strokes and makes gentle circles over the opposite forearm.
text.goal: Gently unload the forearms after hand work.
text.startingPosition: Rest the forearm on a table or thigh.
text.direction: From wrist toward elbow.
text.warning: Stop self-massage with pain, numbness, weakness, dizziness, radiating sensations, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: forearm self-massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The free hand strokes and makes gentle circles over the opposite forearm.

text.title: Hand Self-Massage
text.summary: The thumb of the free hand gently works the palm, then the fingers are lightly stroked.
text.goal: Relax the hands after repetitive activity.
text.startingPosition: Rest the hand comfortably in front of you.
instructions: Make small circles over the fleshy area.
Lightly stroke the back of the hand.
Stroke each finger from base to tip.
text.direction: Over the palm, back of the hand, and fingers.
text.warning: Stop self-massage with pain, numbness, weakness, dizziness, radiating sensations, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: hand self-massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The thumb of the free hand gently works the palm, then the fingers are lightly stroked.

text.title: Thigh Self-Massage
text.summary: The palms make long strokes and gentle circles over the front and outer thigh.
text.goal: Warm the thigh muscles gently after sitting or activity.
text.startingPosition: Sit stably with the leg relaxed.
instructions: Place the palms above the knee.
Do not press the knee joint or groin.
text.direction: From above the knee upward over the thigh.
text.warning: Stop self-massage with pain, numbness, weakness, dizziness, radiating sensations, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: thigh self-massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The palms make long strokes and gentle circles over the front and outer thigh.

text.title: Calf Self-Massage
text.summary: The hands lightly stroke the calf upward without deep pressure.
text.goal: Gently relax the calf muscles after walking.
text.startingPosition: Sit with the leg fully supported.
instructions: Place the hands on the calf above the Achilles tendon.
Do not press the tendon or behind the knee.
text.direction: Upward along the calf.
text.warning: Stop self-massage with pain, numbness, weakness, dizziness, radiating sensations, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: calf self-massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The hands lightly stroke the calf upward without deep pressure.

text.title: Hand Foot Self-Massage
text.summary: The thumb and palm gently work the sole and heel.
text.goal: Relax the foot gently after walking or standing.
text.startingPosition: Sit comfortably and support the foot.
instructions: Stroke the sole from heel to toes.
Add small circles over the arch.
text.direction: From heel to toes and over soft areas of the sole.
text.warning: Stop self-massage with pain, numbness, weakness, dizziness, radiating sensations, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: hand foot self-massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The thumb and palm gently work the sole and heel.

text.title: Scalp Self-Massage
text.summary: The finger pads make small gentle circles over the scalp.
text.goal: Create a short relaxing pause.
text.startingPosition: Sit comfortably and relax the shoulders.
instructions: Place the finger pads on the scalp.
Do not scratch with the nails.
text.direction: Small circles over the scalp.
text.warning: Stop self-massage with pain, numbness, weakness, dizziness, radiating sensations, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: scalp self-massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: The finger pads make small gentle circles over the scalp.

text.title: Desk-Break Neck, Shoulder and Forearm Reset
text.summary: A short sequence of gentle stroking for the shoulders, posterior neck, and forearms.
text.goal: Take a calm break after prolonged static work.
text.startingPosition: Sit stably, lower the shoulders, and place both feet on the floor.
instructions: Gently work the back of the neck.
Stroke the forearm from wrist toward elbow.
text.direction: Over the shoulders, posterior neck, and forearms.
text.warning: Stop self-massage with pain, numbness, weakness, dizziness, radiating sensations, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: desk-break neck, shoulder and forearm reset, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: A short sequence of gentle stroking for the shoulders, posterior neck, and forearms.

text.title: Finishing Self-Massage
text.summary: Several light passes over the chosen area gradually reduce intensity.
text.goal: Finish a short self-massage session calmly.
text.startingPosition: Choose an area you have already worked on.
text.direction: Over the treated area with decreasing pressure.
text.warning: Stop self-massage with pain, numbness, weakness, dizziness, radiating sensations, or other unusual symptoms.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: finishing self-massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: Several light passes over the chosen area gradually reduce intensity.

text.title: Back Massage — 15 Minutes
text.summary: A short sequence of gentle back techniques without deep forceful pressure.
text.goal: Combine basic back techniques into a simple educational routine.
text.startingPosition: The person lies comfortably face down.
text.direction: From gentle warming to moderate work and back to a light finish.
text.warning: This educational routine is not treatment. Do not perform it with contraindications, acute pain, recent injury, inflammation, or worsening wellbeing.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: back massage — 15 minutes, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: A short sequence of gentle back techniques without deep forceful pressure.

text.title: Back Massage — 30 Minutes
text.summary: An extended calm sequence of core back techniques.
text.goal: Combine the basic techniques into a longer educational routine.
text.startingPosition: The person lies comfortably face down.
instructions: 5 min — work around the shoulder blades.
text.direction: Gradually increase intensity in the middle, then finish gently.
text.warning: This educational routine is not treatment. Do not perform it with contraindications, acute pain, recent injury, inflammation, or worsening wellbeing.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: back massage — 30 minutes, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: An extended calm sequence of core back techniques.

text.title: Neck and Shoulders — 15 Minutes
text.summary: A short gentle sequence for the posterior neck and upper shoulders.
text.goal: Combine basic techniques without deep neck pressure.
text.startingPosition: The head is supported, the neck neutral, and the shoulders relaxed.
text.direction: From the posterior neck toward the shoulders, then a gentle finish.
text.warning: This educational routine is not treatment. Do not perform it with contraindications, acute pain, recent injury, inflammation, or worsening wellbeing.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: neck and shoulders — 15 minutes, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: A short gentle sequence for the posterior neck and upper shoulders.

text.title: Leg Massage — 20 Minutes
text.summary: A calm sequence of stroking and moderate kneading for the major leg muscles.
text.goal: Combine basic thigh and lower-leg techniques into a short routine.
text.startingPosition: The legs are fully supported and relaxed.
instructions: 4 min — calf stroking and gentle kneading.
text.direction: Upward over soft tissues while avoiding joints and the back of the knee.
text.warning: This educational routine is not treatment. Do not perform it with contraindications, acute pain, recent injury, inflammation, or worsening wellbeing.

text.telegramCaption: A calm sequence of stroking and moderate kneading for the major leg muscles.

text.title: Relaxing Sequence — 30 Minutes
text.summary: A general gentle routine focused on the back, shoulders, arms, and legs.
text.goal: Combine the main body regions into one calm overview routine.
text.startingPosition: The person is positioned comfortably and each area is exposed and draped in turn.
text.direction: From larger regions to local work with gradually decreasing intensity.
text.warning: This educational routine is not treatment. Do not perform it with contraindications, acute pain, recent injury, inflammation, or worsening wellbeing.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: relaxing sequence — 30 minutes, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: A general gentle routine focused on the back, shoulders, arms, and legs.

text.title: Self-Massage — 10 Minutes
text.summary: A short sequence for the shoulders, forearms, hands, and scalp.
text.goal: Combine gentle techniques into a short daily break.
text.startingPosition: Sit stably, relax the shoulders, and keep the neck neutral.
text.direction: From shoulders to arms and scalp, then a gradual finish.
text.warning: This educational routine is not treatment. Do not perform it with contraindications, acute pain, recent injury, inflammation, or worsening wellbeing.

text.title: When to Postpone Massage
text.summary: A brief list of situations where home massage should be postponed.
text.goal: Help recognize basic stop signs before massage begins.
text.startingPosition: Before massage, assess general wellbeing and the intended area.
instructions: Do not begin during fever or significant acute illness.
Do not massage a recent injury, active inflammation, or damaged skin.
Do not massage an area with unexplained marked swelling, redness, or heat.
New severe pain, numbness, weakness, or dizziness should be assessed first.
text.direction: This is a safety check rather than a movement technique.
tips: Uncertainty is enough reason to reduce intensity or postpone massage.
Safety takes priority over completing a plan.
mistakes: Trying to continue at any cost.
Making overly confident conclusions without professional assessment.
text.warning: This guide is educational and does not replace medical diagnosis or individualized professional advice.
text.imageAlt: Educational diagram: when to postpone massage, without text labels.
text.telegramCaption: A brief list of situations where home massage should be postponed.

text.title: Pressure Scale 1–5
text.summary: A simple scale describes intensity from barely perceptible contact to pronounced pressure.
text.goal: Make pressure easier to understand across cards.
text.startingPosition: Agree beforehand that pain is not the goal of massage.
instructions: 4/5 — pronounced pressure only when appropriate and comfortable.
5/5 — not used as a routine target in this home guide.
text.direction: Increase pressure gradually.
tips: Uncertainty is enough reason to reduce intensity or postpone massage.
Safety takes priority over completing a plan.
mistakes: Trying to continue at any cost.

text.title: Consent and Personal Boundaries
text.summary: Clear consent should cover the massage itself, intended areas, and level of contact.
text.goal: Make respect for boundaries part of safe practice.
text.startingPosition: Discuss working areas before beginning.
instructions: Ask whether massage is comfortable at all.
Clarify which areas may or may not be touched.
Obtain specific consent before more personal areas.
text.direction: This is a communication rule rather than movement direction.
tips: Uncertainty is enough reason to reduce intensity or postpone massage.

text.title: Positioning and Support
text.summary: Comfortable neutral positioning and support for the head, arms, and legs reduce unnecessary tension.
text.goal: Create stable, comfortable positioning before technique begins.
text.startingPosition: Use pillows, bolsters, or folded towels as needed.
instructions: Support the head and neck neutrally.
Support a limb if it is tensing.
Do not hold joints at end range.
Change position if numbness or discomfort appears.
text.direction: Establish stable positioning first.
tips: Uncertainty is enough reason to reduce intensity or postpone massage.

text.title: Skin, Oil, and Glide
text.summary: Oil or cream should reduce unnecessary friction without hiding skin damage.
text.goal: Maintain comfortable glide and safe hand control.
text.startingPosition: Inspect the skin and ask about product sensitivity.
instructions: Do not apply product to damaged or inflamed skin.
Use a small amount of a neutral product.
Stop if burning, itching, or rash appears.
text.direction: Spread product in a thin even layer.

text.title: One-Sided Leg Swelling and Pain
text.summary: One-sided swelling, redness, warmth, and calf pain are reasons not to massage the leg until medically assessed.
text.goal: Help recognize an important stop sign before leg massage.
text.startingPosition: Compare both legs and notice new asymmetry.
instructions: Do not massage a painful or noticeably swollen leg.
Do not deeply knead a painful calf.
Seek medical care if symptoms are sudden or pronounced.
text.direction: Massage is not performed.
tips: Uncertainty is enough reason to reduce intensity or postpone massage.
Safety takes priority over completing a plan.

text.title: Feedback During Massage
text.summary: Comfort is best checked with brief questions and observation throughout the session.
text.goal: Make feedback a continuous part of safe practice.
text.startingPosition: Agree beforehand that pain, numbness, dizziness, or discomfort should be reported.
instructions: Ask about pressure after the first passes.
Reduce intensity if the person tenses.
Stop with pain, numbness, or dizziness.
Do not encourage someone to tolerate pain.
text.direction: This rule applies throughout the session.
